long_biography.plain_text:
Six-year-old Warner Peacock began learning the car trade on rural Florida roads, accompanying his grandfather, a Ford salesman, as he showed recent trade-ins to local families. Peacock later worked in his father's dealership through high school and college and studied accounting at Florida State University. He then learned dealership management under mentor Don Mealey before starting stores of his own.

He founded Peacock Automotive and built it into a multi-state network representing mass-market and luxury marques. A 2021 agreement transferred eleven dealerships and a collision centre to AutoNation; Peacock retained his Maitland Ford operation until its 2025 sale to Holler-Classic. Away from vehicle retail, he has developed shopping centres, restaurant sites, bank branches and residential communities, and supported Florida State athletic scholarships.

uncertainties.detail: Peacock sold eleven dealerships to AutoNation in 2021 and his retained Ford outlet to Holler-Classic in 2025. Public sources document substantial property interests but do not disclose a complete current portfolio or valuation split. Automotive is therefore retained as the best-supported primary-industry fallback, not asserted as a current operating dealership business.

Institutional profiles consistently call Peacock a Tallahassee native and say he grew up there, supporting the proposed place of birth. No authoritative public source located in this research states his exact birth day, month or year, so those fields remain unproposed.

A South Carolina legislative journal identifies him as William ‘Warner’ Peacock, while Florida corporate records use W. Warner Peacock and the source record stores Warner as the first name. Because the owner schema's placement of William would be ambiguous and could duplicate his call name, no middle-name correction is proposed.

No identity-secure personal LinkedIn, Instagram, personal website or current canonical company website was found. Former dealership domains no longer represent Peacock after the 2021 and 2025 sales, so no social link is proposed.

Exact-name, company-name and site-restricted searches found no dedicated Forbes profile for Warner Peacock. Results dominated by the Peacock media brand and unrelated Warner-named figures were excluded.

No independent public page located in this research names Warner Peacock in connection with Namastay under its current name. The match rests on the upstream record's QTR association, YachtBuyer's independent documentation of QTR as Namastay's former name and a strong exact-person business and geography match; this exceeds the threshold but remains below certainty.

Automotive dealerships captures Peacock's defining wealth platform, while Property developer captures a separate, repeatedly documented occupation across multiple property types. Broader banking, philanthropy and university-governance tags were not added because the evidence does not establish equally defining identities under the active catalogue contracts.
